## The focused lane profile

1. Write the story's scenarios first (test-first or characterization-first, as the plan says). Every test must assert
   something.
2. Commit, then run the gates: `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py gate <key>`. It runs, in order:
   - `python3 -B scripts/validate-registry.py`
   - `python3 -B scripts/update-provenance.py --check`
   and records the result against your HEAD. The hand-off needs a passing run at the head you hand off.
3. Run the story's in-app checks, if the repository declares them (see In-app checks).
4. Review (see Review) until every lens approves, within 4 rounds. At the bound, stop and report the blocker
   to the lead.
5. Compounding: note anything reusable for the lead in the PR body or the hand-off's `--findings`.
6. Push your own branch and open its draft PR into `main`: `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py push <key>`, then
   `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py open-pr <key> --title "<key>: <summary>" --body-file <file>` (Summary, Why, Validation; the tracker link
   is added if missing). Both refuse what the authority below doesn't grant.

   **Authority.** the operator gave lanes authority on 2026-11-11 to push your own `claude/<key>` branch, with `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py push <key>`, and open its draft pull request into `main`, with `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py open-pr`. That is all: never push any other branch, never force-push, never merge, and never mark a pull request ready or approve one. The lead's merge queue merges.
7. Hand off (see Hand-off).

The review must see the final code, and the gates and in-app checks must have run on it. If anything changes after a
round, run another round; re-run the gates at the new head, and the in-app checks if shipped files changed.

## Review

Lenses `lens.outcome-correctness`, `lens.adversarial-testing`, through `obtain-review`/`review-work`, realized by host convention as reviewers the lane starts and
resumes. `run-delivery` does the mechanical part.

1. Before round 1, fill in "Evidence so far" in `.orchestration/review/<key>/context.md`. `review-prepare` seeds it
   from the plan the first time it runs and refuses until you replace the TODO line. Update it before each later round.
2. `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py review-prepare <key> --round <n>` makes one private, prepared checkout per lens at your HEAD and one filled
   round brief per lens. Commit first: it refuses uncommitted or untracked files.
3. Round 1: start one reviewer per lens in parallel with the prompts it prints, and keep track of each. Later rounds:
   resume the same reviewers with the new prompts. Save each final JSON message, exactly as returned, to the result path it
   printed. Never write or edit a result yourself. A prepared round can't be prepared again: reduce it. If you must
   discard it (the candidate was wrong, say), `--restart` does, and the lead has to accept every restart.
4. `python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py review-reduce <key> --round <n>` checks each result against its brief, assembles the round file, checks it
   with the release's own validator, journals the round, removes the lens checkouts, and prints the verdict, the open
   and deferred findings, and the tracker post. A result that doesn't match its brief is kept as an attempt and the
   round refused: re-run only that lens with the same brief; the other results stand. Attempts are recorded.
5. Fix the blocking findings, commit, and go to step 2 with the next round. At the bound without alignment the round
   is `blocked`: stop and tell the lead (a grace round, `--grace`, needs the lead's say-so).
6. If you ever lose your review folder (a recreated checkout, say), tell the lead: the lead-side log still has your
   earlier preparations, and the lead decides on them at acceptance.

Triage: blocking findings, every P0 and every P1 a lens files open, are always fixed in the lane. Lenses file P2/P3 as
deferred, with what the follow-up must say, and a P1 too when a verification round files it new outside the delta,
listing its id in `lateFindings`; a P0 is never deferred. Fix the cheap deferrals in the lane anyway, and pass the
expensive ones to the lead with `--findings`. A finding first raised in a later round, against code an earlier round
approved, is judged on scope before it blocks.

## Hand-off

`python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/run-delivery/scripts/run_delivery.py handoff <key> --pr <PR link> [--checks <catalogue ids you ran>] [--findings "<expensive non-blocking findings>"] [--blocked <name>=<reason> ...]`

`--checks` names the test modules you ran by the binding's catalogue ids, comma-separated: the lead's acceptance proposes
them for the candidate's checks.

Every `--blocked` item, and every restarted review round, is the lead's decision: the lead accepts each one by
name, or sends the story back. It refuses unless the checkout is clean (untracked files included), your branch on `origin` is at HEAD, the PR is
open from your branch into `main`, the last round has every lens approving exactly that head, the gates
passed at it, and the in-app evidence is complete and current. Then it captures the review rounds, hands off to the
record, and prints the hand-off message and the tracker post. Send the lead that message, word for word. Don't merge
or release. The lead verifies the claims and accepts; the merge queue merges after syncing your branch with the base.

## Tracker updates

The commands make the start, review and hand-off posts and moves, or print them when the tracker is yours to update
by hand: make exactly what a command prints as a "Tracker move" or "Tracker post", with your tracker tools, and never
repeat by hand what a command says it made. `handoff` posts the hand-off update itself when the tracker has a
publisher; if the tracker refuses it, the hand-off still stands and the publisher posts it later. Post on your own
story with your tracker tools at each decision you make (what and why), at each review round (`review-reduce`
prints the text), and at each finding you pass to the lead. One attempt each, never a gate.

Don't move your story's status: this repository gives lanes no status moves.

## Focus

Say what you're doing as it changes, with the installed release's state tool:
`python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/orchestrate-work/scripts/delivery_state.py --dir /Users/kwamina/code/agent-skills/.orchestration/lanes/V26-3406/.orchestration/state focus --lane <lane> --text "<what you are doing>" [--state working|reviewing|blocked] [--waiting-on <who>]`.
`review-prepare` sets `reviewing` for you.

If a product run builds your story, bind its run id at start, before your first round:
`python3 -B .agent-skills/current/skills/orchestrate-work/scripts/delivery_state.py --dir /Users/kwamina/code/agent-skills/.orchestration/lanes/V26-3406/.orchestration/state bind-run --lane <lane> --subject <key> --run <run id>`.
The live view then shows the run's rounds before your hand-off, and the hand-off keeps the run. A story with no run binds none.

## Your turn

End your turn only to hand off, to report yourself blocked, or to ask the lead. Never end it just to wait for a
reviewer, the gates, an in-app check or the pipeline: wait inside the turn. Run long commands in the background and
wait for them, resume your reviewers and wait for their results, and use `pr-review <key> --wait`.

## Questions

Escalate only to the lead, never to the user: set `focus --text "<your one short question>" --state blocked --waiting-on
lead`, so the lead's `wait` sees it and carries the question, then send the question and stop. The lead answers, or takes
it to the user. When the answer comes, set `focus --text "<what you are doing>" --state working --waiting-on ""` before
going on.

## Local load

Run at most 4 local test workers. Stop only processes you started, by the pid you
recorded, never by pattern.

## Delivery notes

## This delivery's own rules

The approved plan's Decisions are binding. These notes add what the plan leaves to the lead.

**Authority.** Lanes may push their story branches and open draft pull requests into `main`, as the delivery's grant states. No lane
merges, marks a pull request ready, tags, or applies a release, except V26-3410's apply of the candidate the lead has tagged.

**No deferrals.** Nothing found in this delivery is deferred. Every finding is fixed in the story that found it, before hand-off,
whatever its severity, cost or round. This overrides the brief's Triage and Hand-off sections where they say otherwise:
- A P2 or P3 a lens files as deferred is fixed in the lane, the same as a blocking finding.
- A late P1 listed in `lateFindings` is fixed too.
- A note a lens leaves in its evidence (for example "P2, not filed") is a finding, and is fixed.
- Nothing goes to the lead as an expensive non-blocking finding: `handoff` carries no `--findings`, and no follow-up item is filed
  for anything this delivery found.

If a fix needs a file outside your `owns`, ask the lead to move it to you. If a fix is out of reach (it needs an operator decision, or
another epic's change), stop and tell the lead before hand-off. Don't hand off around it.

**Criteria come from the tracker items.** Each item's Acceptance Criteria were created from its plan section and then gained the rows
the plan review's second round left as notes. Where the two differ, the tracker item is the fuller one and binds:
- V26-3409 has an orientation row for every `SessionStart` source (`startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact` and `fork`), and one with
  the payload's `cwd` reached through a symlink.
- V26-3410's live check runs the installed command unchanged behind a logging wrapper that logs stdin first.

**Pins that will go stale.** Re-derive the pins your change makes stale, as the plan's Units and order lists them, and name each in your
hand-off. `provenance.lock.json` is lane 2's: add `skills/run-delivery/hooks.json` as an output by hand, then digest it with the writer.

**No real host in rows.** No test starts a Claude Code session or writes `.claude/settings.json` in the repository root. Every lifecycle
and hook row works in its own temporary folder with its own state directory.

**Lane 1: V26-3407, then V26-3408, then V26-3410 in tier 2.** V26-3410 starts only when the lead says the minor candidate is tagged and
published; it applies it and turns `lead.may-stop` to `enforce` in one change, and records the live check on the epic before hand-off.

**Lane 2: V26-3270, then V26-3409.** V26-3409 starts once V26-3407 has merged, since it needs the manifest schema and the dispatcher.
